questions.question: The rainbow—a natural spectrum visible in the sky after rain—is primarily caused by which action of water droplets on sunlight?

options.text: Refraction and dispersion, followed by internal reflection, and then finally refraction
Bending of light due to change in air density

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**अपवर्तन और परिक्षेपण, उसके बाद आंतरिक परावर्तन, और फिर अंतिम अपवर्तन**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **इंद्रधनुष** एक प्राकृतिक **स्पेक्ट्रम** है जो वर्षा के बाद आकाश में दिखाई देता है। यह वातावरण में मौजूद पानी की छोटी बूंदों द्वारा **सूर्य के प्रकाश के परिक्षेपण** (Dispersion) के कारण होता है।
 
• जब सूर्य का प्रकाश पानी की एक बूंद में प्रवेश करता है, तो यह सबसे पहले **अपवर्तन** (Refraction) से गुजरता है और सात रंगों में विभाजित हो जाता है, जिसे **परिक्षेपण** कहा जाता है। ***अतः, विकल्प 2 में वर्णित प्रक्रिया का प्रारंभिक चरण सही है।***
 
• बूंद के भीतर जाने के बाद, प्रकाश की किरणें बूंद की पीछे की सतह से टकराती हैं और **आंतरिक परावर्तन** (Internal Reflection) का अनुभव करती हैं।
 
• अंत में, जब प्रकाश की किरणें पानी की बूंद से बाहर निकलती हैं, तो वे एक बार फिर **अपवर्तित** होती हैं और प्रेक्षक की आंखों तक पहुँचती हैं, जिससे एक रंगीन चाप (Arc) दिखाई देता है।
 
• इंद्रधनुष हमेशा **सूर्य की विपरीत दिशा** में बनता है। इसमें पानी की बूंदें एक छोटे **प्रिज्म** की तरह कार्य करती हैं।

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **परिक्षेपण (Dispersion):** श्वेत प्रकाश का उसके घटक रंगों (लाल, नारंगी, पीला, हरा, नीला, जामुनी और बैंगनी - **VIBGYOR**) में विभाजित होने की प्रक्रिया को परिक्षेपण कहा जाता है। लाल रंग का **तरंगदैर्घ्य (Wave length)** सबसे अधिक होता है और यह सबसे कम झुकता है, जबकि बैंगनी रंग का तरंगदैर्घ्य सबसे कम होता है और यह सबसे अधिक झुकता है।
 
• **अपवर्तन (Refraction):** जब प्रकाश की किरण एक माध्यम से दूसरे माध्यम (जैसे वायु से जल) में प्रवेश करती है, तो इसकी **गति (Speed)** बदल जाती है, जिससे यह अपने पथ से विचलित हो जाती है। इसे अपवर्तन कहते हैं।
 
• **आंतरिक परावर्तन (Internal Reflection):** इंद्रधनुष के मामले में, बूंद के भीतर प्रकाश का पूर्ण आंतरिक परावर्तन (TIR) नहीं बल्कि **आंतरिक परावर्तन** होता है, क्योंकि कुछ प्रकाश बूंद से बाहर भी निकल जाता है।
 
• **प्राथमिक इंद्रधनुष (Primary Rainbow):** यह तब बनता है जब प्रकाश की किरण बूंद के अंदर **एक बार आंतरिक परावर्तन** करती है। इसमें लाल रंग बाहरी किनारे पर और बैंगनी रंग आंतरिक किनारे पर होता है। इसकी कोणीय त्रिज्या लगभग **40° से 42°** होती है।

__

• **सर आइजैक न्यूटन** ने सबसे पहले यह प्रदर्शित किया था कि सूर्य का प्रकाश सात रंगों से मिलकर बना है।
 
• हवाई जहाज से देखने पर इंद्रधनुष अक्सर एक **पूर्ण वृत्त (Full Circle)** के रूप में दिखाई देता है, क्योंकि जमीन क्षितिज (Horizon) को बाधित नहीं करती है।
 
• **प्रकीर्णन (Scattering):** यह धूल के कणों या गैस के अणुओं द्वारा प्रकाश के फैलने की घटना है (जैसे आकाश का नीला रंग), लेकिन यह इंद्रधनुष के निर्माण का मुख्य कारण नहीं है। ***अतः, कथन 3 गलत है।***

questions.question: Which of the following refining methods is most important commercially?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chemical methods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Refining** is the final process in **metallurgy** used to obtain metals of **high purity** from the crude metal extracted through reduction.
 
• **Chemical methods** of refining are commercially highly significant because they allow for the production of **ultra-high-purity metals** required in modern industrial applications. ***Hence, the correct answer is Chemical methods.***
 
• One major chemical refining technique is **Vapour Phase Refining**, which involves converting the metal into a **volatile compound** and then decomposing it to give pure metal. This includes the **Mond Process** and the **Van Arkel Method**.
 
• In the **Mond Process**, **Nickel** is refined by reacting it with **Carbon Monoxide** at **330-350 K** to form **Nickel Tetracarbonyl**, which is then decomposed at higher temperatures (**450-470 K**) to recover pure **Nickel**.
 
• The **Van Arkel Method** is used for refining metals like **Zirconium** and **Titanium** by removing oxygen and nitrogen impurities through the formation of volatile **iodides**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Physical Methods:**

 
 
• **Distillation**: Used for metals with **low boiling points** such as **Zinc**, **Mercury**, and **Cadmium**. The impure metal is evaporated to obtain pure metal as distillate.
 
• **Liquation**: Used for metals with **low melting points** compared to their impurities, such as **Tin** (**Sn**) and **Lead** (**Pb**). The metal is melted on a sloping hearth to separate it from high-melting impurities.
 
 
 
• **Electrochemical Refining:**
 
 
• In this process, the **impure metal** serves as the **anode**, and a strip of **pure metal** serves as the **cathode**.
 
• It is widely used for the commercial purification of **Copper**, **Zinc**, **Tin**, **Silver**, and **Gold**.
 
• During the electrolysis of **Copper**, impurities like **Antimony**, **Selenium**, and **Tellurium** settle down as **anode mud**.
 
 
 
• **Zone Refining (Fractional Crystallization):**
 
 
• This method is based on the principle that **impurities** are more soluble in the **molten state** than in the **solid state** of the metal.
 
• It is commercially essential for producing **semiconductors** of very high purity, such as **Germanium**, **Silicon**, **Boron**, **Gallium**, and **Indium**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chromatographic Methods:** This chemical technique is based on the principle of **differential adsorption**. It is used when the impurities and the metal have similar chemical properties, allowing for purification in **micro-quantities**.
 
• **Oxidative Refining:** Processes like **Cupellation** (for **Silver**) and **Bessemerization** (for **Iron/Steel**) involve the oxidation of impurities to separate them from the metal.
 
• The choice of refining method depends largely on the **nature of the metal** and the **type of impurities** present. For commercial electronics and aerospace components, **chemical** and **electrochemical** methods are indispensable.

1. Bud formation </f
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 – 3 – 2 – 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Budding (मुकुलन)** is a form of **asexual reproduction** in which a new organism develops from an outgrowth or **bud** due to cell division at one particular site.
 
• **Bud formation (मुकुल निर्माण):** The process begins when a small protuberance or bulb-like projection, called a **bud**, develops on the body of the parent organism. ***Hence, step 1 is the first stage.***
 
• **Nuclear division (केन्द्रक विभाजन):** Once the bud is formed, the **nucleus** of the parent cell undergoes division (mitosis). One of the daughter nuclei then migrates into the developing bud. ***Hence, step 3 is the second stage.***
 
• **Cytoplasmic division (कोशिकाद्रव्य विभाजन):** Following nuclear division, the **cytoplasm** starts to divide. The bud receives a portion of the parent's cytoplasm, and a constriction forms between the parent body and the bud. ***Hence, step 2 is the third stage.***
 
• **Separation of the bud (मुकुल का पृथक्करण):** In the final stage, the bud grows to a certain size and eventually **detaches** from the parent body to become an independent individual. ***Hence, step 4 is the fourth stage.***
 
• Therefore, the most suitable sequence for the process of budding in organisms is **1 (Bud formation) → 3 (Nuclear division) → 2 (Cytoplasmic division) → 4 (Separation)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Organisms using Budding:**

 
 
• **Yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae):** A **unicellular fungus** where budding is the primary mode of reproduction. In some cases, buds do not separate immediately and form a **chain of buds**.
 
• **Hydra:** A **multicellular freshwater animal**. In Hydra, a bud develops as an outgrowth due to repeated cell division at a specific site. These buds develop into tiny individuals and, when fully mature, detach from the parent body.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Asexual Reproduction:**
 
 
• It involves only a **single parent**.
 
• There is no **fusion of gametes** (sperm and egg).
 
• The offspring produced are **genetically identical** to the parent, often referred to as **clones**.
 
• This process is relatively **rapid** compared to sexual reproduction, allowing for quick population growth.
 
 
 
• **Cellular Terms:**
 
 
• **Karyokinesis:** The technical term for **nuclear division**. In budding, it ensures that the new individual receives the necessary genetic information.
 
• **Cytokinesis:** The technical term for **cytoplasmic division**, which physically separates the new cell or organism from the parent.
 
 
 
• **Difference from Binary Fission:** Unlike **binary fission** (seen in **Amoeba**), where the parent cell divides into two equal halves and the parent identity is lost, in **budding**, the parent organism remains intact after the smaller bud detaches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Environmental Factors:** Budding usually occurs when **nutrients** are abundant and environmental conditions are favorable for growth.
 
• **Internal Budding:** While most budding is external, some organisms like **sponges** undergo internal budding by forming **gemmules** to survive harsh conditions.
 
• **Regenerative Cells:** In multicellular organisms like Hydra, budding relies on the presence of **regenerative cells** that have the capacity to divide and differentiate into various cell types.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about acceleration is correct?

options.text: Acceleration is negative when it acts opposite to the direction of velocity.
Acceleration is always positive regardless of its direction.
The SI unit of acceleration is m/s.
Acceleration is positive when it acts opposite to the direction of velocity.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**त्वरण तब ऋणात्मक होता है जब यह वेग की दिशा के विपरीत कार्य करता है।**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acceleration** is defined as the **rate of change of velocity** of an object with respect to **time**. It is a **vector quantity**, meaning it possesses both **magnitude** and **direction**.
 
• Statement 1: **Acceleration** is considered **negative** when it acts in the **opposite direction** of the **velocity**. This condition leads to a decrease in the speed of the object, a phenomenon commonly known as **retardation** or **deceleration**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Statement 2: The sign of **acceleration** depends on the coordinate system and the change in **velocity**. It can be **positive**, **negative**, or **zero**. It is not always positive. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 3: The **SI unit** of **velocity** is **m/s** (meters per second). However, **acceleration** is the change in **velocity** over **time**, making its **SI unit** **m/s²** (meters per second squared). ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 4: When **acceleration** is in the **same direction** as the **velocity**, it is **positive**, causing the object's speed to increase. If it is **opposite** to the **velocity**, it is **negative**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uniform and Non-Uniform Acceleration:**

 
 
• If an object's **velocity** changes by an **equal amount** in **equal intervals of time**, it is said to have **uniform acceleration**. A common example is an object in **free fall** near the **Earth's surface**, where acceleration due to **gravity** is approximately **9.8 m/s²**.

• **Mathematical Formula:**

For instance, in **uniform circular motion**, the **acceleration** (centripetal) is always directed toward the **center**, which is **perpendicular** to the **tangential velocity**.
 
• **Zero Acceleration:** When an object moves with a **constant velocity** (constant speed in a straight line), the **change in velocity** is **zero**, and therefore, the **acceleration** is **0 m/s²**.

Because the Earth's rotation slows down during sunrise and sunset
Due to the gravitational effect of the Moon on sunlight

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atmospheric Refraction** is the phenomenon where **Light Rays** from the **Sun** bend as they pass through different layers of the **Earth's Atmosphere**.
 
• The **Density** of the atmosphere is not uniform; it is **Denser** near the surface and becomes **Rarer** with **Altitude**. This variation in density leads to a variation in the **Refractive Index**.
 
• When sunlight enters the Earth's atmosphere, it travels from a **Vacuum** (rarer medium) into the air (denser medium), causing the light to bend towards the **Normal**.
 
• Due to this continuous **Refraction**, the **Sun** appears to be slightly higher than its actual position when it is near the **Horizon**.
 
• As a result, we can see the Sun about **2 minutes** before the **Actual Sunrise** (when the Sun is still below the horizon) and for about **2 minutes** after the **Actual Sunset**. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• The idea that the Sun moves faster near the horizon is a common **Optical Illusion** but is physically incorrect as the **Earth's Angular Velocity** remains constant. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Rotation of the Earth** is a uniform process at approximately **1,670 km/h** at the equator and does not slow down during specific times of the day. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Gravitational Effect** of the **Moon** on light (Gravitational Lensing) is negligible in the context of Earth's local atmosphere and does not contribute to the timing of sunrise or sunset. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Total Day Length:** Because of the **2-minute** advance in sunrise and **2-minute** delay in sunset, the total duration of **Daylight** is increased by approximately **4 minutes**.
 
• **Twinkling of Stars:** This is another major application of **Atmospheric Refraction**. Since stars are point sources of light, the continuous change in the **Atmosphere's Density** causes the **Apparent Position** of the star to fluctuate, which our eyes perceive as **Twinkling**.
 
• **Advanced Sunrise/Delayed Sunset Facts:** These phenomena occur every day but are most noticeable in flat areas like **Deserts** or over the **Ocean** where the **Horizon** is clearly visible.

The **Reddish Color** of the Sun at dawn and dusk is due to **Rayleigh Scattering**, where shorter wavelengths (blue) are scattered away, leaving longer wavelengths (red).
 
• **Snell's Law:** The mathematical principle behind this bending is **Snell's Law**, which states that the ratio of the sines of the angles of incidence and refraction is equivalent to the ratio of phase velocities in the two media.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct series of events when a vibrating body produces sound?

options.text: Sound → Vibration → Vibration in the medium → Detection by the ear
Vibration → Vibration in the particles of the medium → Propagation of sound wave → Sound is heard

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vibration → Vibration in the particles of the medium → Propagation of sound wave → Sound is heard**__ .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sound production always begins with **the vibration of an object. When an object vibrates, it releases energy that spreads into the surrounding environment.**
 
• Once the object begins to vibrate, it creates a disturbance in **the particles of the medium** it comes into contact with . These particles begin to vibrate about their mean position.
 
• This disturbance is transferred from one particle to another, causing **the propagation of a sound wave** . In this case, the particles of the medium themselves do not move from one place to another, but only transfer energy. ***Therefore, the sequence of events given in option 2 is correct.***
 
• When this transmitted sound wave reaches our ear, it creates vibrations in the eardrum, which are processed by the brain and we **hear sound** .
 
• Option 1 is incorrect because 'sound' is the result of the process, not its origin. Options 3 and 4 are also incorrect because **electricity** , **light,** or **heat** are not essential intermediate steps in normal sound production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Sound** : Sound is a **mechanical wave** . It requires a physical medium to travel. It cannot travel in **a vacuum because there are no particles to transmit vibrations.**
 
• **Effect of the medium** : The speed of sound depends on the density and elasticity of the medium. The speed of sound is highest in **solids** , followed by **liquids** , and lowest in **gases** . For example, the speed of sound in air at **0°C** is approximately **331 m/s .**
 
• **Longitudinal Waves** : Sound waves are longitudinal, meaning that the particles of the medium vibrate **parallel** to the direction of propagation. This creates regions of **compression** and **rarefaction .**
 
• **Frequency and Pitch** : The number of vibrations per second is called **frequency , measured in ****hertz (Hz)** . Higher frequency means higher pitch (such as children's or women's voices).
 
• **Audible Range** : The human ear can normally hear frequencies between **20 Hz and 20,000 Hz** . Sounds below 20 Hz are called **infrasonic** , and those above 20,000 Hz are called **ultrasonic .**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Amplitude of vibration** : The maximum displacement of the vibration is called **the amplitude** . It determines **the loudness of the sound. A higher amplitude means a louder sound.**
 
• **Decibel (dB)** : The unit of measurement for sound intensity is **the decibel . Sounds over ****80 dB** are generally considered noise that can be harmful to health.
 
• **Effect of Temperature** : As **the temperature** of the medium increases, the speed of sound also increases. This is why sound travels faster in warm air than in cold air.

questions.question: When a current of 1 A flows through an electric geyser for 10 seconds, 100 J of heat is generated. What is the resistance of the geyser?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10 Ω**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The amount of heat produced in a conductor when an electric current passes through it is governed by **Joule’s Law of Heating**. According to this law, the heat generated (**H**) is directly proportional to the square of the **current** (**I**), the **resistance** (**R**) of the conductor, and the **time** (**t**) for which the current flows.
 
• The mathematical expression for this law is **H = I²Rt**. In this equation, **H** is measured in **Joules** (**J**), **I** in **Amperes** (**A**), **R** in **Ohms** (**Ω**), and **t** in **seconds** (**s**).
 
• In the given problem, the current (**I**) is **1 A**, the time (**t**) is **10 seconds**, and the heat produced (**H**) is **100 J**.
 
• To find the resistance, we rearrange the formula to **R = H / (I²t)**. Substituting the known values: **R = 100 / (1² × 10)**.
 
• This simplifies to **R = 100 / 10**, which equals **10 Ω**. ***Hence, the resistance of the geyser is 10 Ω, making option 1 the correct answer.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electric Geyser:** It is an appliance that converts **electrical energy** into **heat energy**. It uses a **heating element** made of materials with **high resistance** and **high melting point**, such as **Nichrome** (an alloy of nickel and chromium).
 
• **Resistance (R):** It is the property of a conductor to oppose the flow of **electric current**. The **SI unit** of resistance is the **Ohm**, named after the German physicist **Georg Simon Ohm**. Resistance depends on the **length**, **area of cross-section**, **nature of the material**, and **temperature**.
 
• **Current (I):** It is defined as the **rate of flow of electric charge** through a cross-section of a conductor. Its **SI unit** is the **Ampere** (**A**), and it is measured using an instrument called an **ammeter**.
 
• **Electrical Energy and Power:** Power (**P**) is the rate at which electrical energy is consumed, given by **P = VI** or **P = I²R**. Heat (**H**) is simply the power multiplied by time (**H = P × t**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Joule's Law Discovery:** The heating effect of current was studied experimentally by **James Prescott Joule** in the year **1841**. It is a fundamental principle used in domestic appliances like **electric irons**, **toasters**, **ovens**, and **heaters**.
 
• **Units Consistency:** When solving numerical problems related to **Joule's Law**, it is crucial to ensure that **time** is always in **seconds**. If time is given in minutes or hours, it must be converted (**1 minute = 60 seconds**).
 
• **Practical Application:** In a **geyser**, the resistance is designed such that for a standard **voltage** (usually **220V** in India), the current flowing through it produces enough heat to raise the water temperature efficiently within a reasonable **time**.
 
• **Safety Feature:** Most heating appliances include a **thermostat** to break the circuit once a certain temperature is reached, preventing damage due to excessive heat production.

questions.question: Which enzyme is responsible for breaking down complex sugar molecules into simple glucose in humans?

The correct answer is __**Amylase**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amylase** is the primary enzyme responsible for the chemical **breakdown of complex carbohydrates** (starch) into **simple sugars** such as **maltose** and **glucose**.
 
• In humans, this digestive process begins in the **mouth**, where **salivary amylase** (also known as **ptyalin**) is secreted by the **salivary glands**.
 
• The **pancreas** also produces **pancreatic amylase**, which is released into the **small intestine** to further digest any remaining starch into **monosaccharides** for absorption.
 
• **Pepsin** is an enzyme produced in the **stomach** specifically for the digestion of **proteins** into **peptides**. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Bile Juice** is produced by the **liver** and stored in the **gallbladder**; it does not contain enzymes but helps in the **emulsification of fats**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Lipase** is an enzyme responsible for breaking down **fats (lipids)** into **fatty acids** and **glycerol**. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Carbohydrate Digestion**:

 
 
• It is a multi-step process that starts in the **oral cavity**. About **30% of starch** is hydrolyzed in the mouth by **salivary amylase** at an optimum **pH of 6.8**.
 
• The final digestion occurs in the **small intestine** where enzymes like **maltase**, **sucrase**, and **lactase** convert disaccharides into **glucose**, **fructose**, and **galactose**.
 
 
 
• **Pepsin and Protein Digestion**:
 
 
• The **stomach mucosa** contains gastric glands that secrete **proenzyme pepsinogen**.
 
• On exposure to **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)**, pepsinogen is converted into the active enzyme **Pepsin**, which works best in an **acidic pH** of about **1.8**.
 
 
 
• **Role of Lipase**:
 
 
• **Lipases** are secreted by the **pancreas** (steapsin) and in small amounts by the **stomach** (gastric lipase).
 
• They require the presence of **bile salts** to increase the surface area of fat droplets through **emulsification**.
 
 
 
• **Bile Juice Functions**:
 
 
• **Bile** contains **bile pigments** (bilirubin and biliverdin), **bile salts**, cholesterol, and phospholipids.
 
• It neutralizes the **acidic chyme** coming from the stomach and makes the medium **alkaline** for the action of **pancreatic enzymes**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Location of Secretion**: **Salivary Amylase** is secreted in the **mouth**, while **Pancreatic Amylase** is secreted in the **duodenum**.
 
• **End Products**: The ultimate goal of **Amylase** activity is to provide the body with **Glucose**, which is the primary **energy source** for **cellular respiration**.
 
• **Enzyme Specificity**: Enzymes are highly specific; **Amylase** only acts on **alpha-1,4-glycosidic bonds** in starch and cannot digest **cellulose** due to the lack of **cellulase** in humans.

Choose the correct option regarding the following two statements (denoted as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). 

**Assertion (A):** Precipitation reactions form soluble salts. 

**Reason (R):** Precipitation reactions involve exchange of ions in solution.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is false, but R is true.
Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A)** states that precipitation reactions form soluble salts. This statement is **false** because **a precipitation reaction** is a chemical process in which two aqueous solutions react to form an **insoluble solid called ****a precipitate** . Soluble salts dissolve in water, while the precipitate separates. ***Therefore, Assertion (A) is false.***
 
• **Reason (R)** states that precipitation reactions involve the exchange of ions in solution. This statement is **true** . Most precipitation reactions are examples of **double displacement reactions , where ****ions** are exchanged between the reactants . ***Therefore, Reason (R) is true.***
 
• When aqueous solutions of two ionic compounds are mixed, their **cations** and **anions** change places. If one of the new compounds is **insoluble** in water , it settles to the bottom as a solid.
 
• As a well-known example, when solutions of **sodium sulphate** and **barium chloride** are mixed, a white precipitate of **barium sulphate (BaSO4)** is formed and **sodium chloride (NaCl)** remains in the solution.
 
• ***Therefore, the correct answer is A is false, but R is true.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Precipitation Reaction:** This is a reaction that results in the formation of **an insoluble salt** . It is often used in laboratories to identify the presence of a particular ion.

questions.question: Which of the following reactions is an example of a precipitation reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**AgNO3 + NaCl → AgCl↓ + NaNO3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **precipitation reaction** is a type of chemical reaction in which **two soluble salts** in aqueous solution combine to form one or more **insoluble products**, called a **precipitate**.
 
• In the reaction **AgNO3 + NaCl → AgCl↓ + NaNO3**, aqueous **Silver Nitrate** reacts with aqueous **Sodium Chloride** to form **Silver Chloride** and **Sodium Nitrate**. The **Silver Chloride (AgCl)** is insoluble in water and settles down as a **white precipitate**. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• This reaction is also a classic example of a **double displacement reaction**, where the **Silver (Ag+)** and **Sodium (Na+)** cations exchange their respective **Nitrate (NO3-)** and **Chloride (Cl-)** anions.
 
• The **downward arrow (↓)** next to a chemical formula in an equation specifically denotes the formation of a **precipitate**, indicating that the substance has crashed out of the solution as a **solid**.
 
• Precipitation reactions are essential in **qualitative inorganic analysis** to identify various **ions** present in a solution based on the **color** and **solubility** of the precipitate formed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• In the reaction **CaCO3 → CaO + CO2↑**, **Calcium Carbonate** (limestone) breaks down into **Calcium Oxide** (quicklime) and **Carbon Dioxide** gas upon heating.
 
• This is a **thermal decomposition reaction**. The **upward arrow (↑)** indicates the evolution of a **gas**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Single Displacement Reaction:**
 
 
• The reaction **Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2↑** involves **Zinc** metal reacting with **Sulfuric Acid**.
 
• Since **Zinc** is more reactive than **Hydrogen**, it displaces hydrogen from the acid to form **Zinc Sulfate** and **Hydrogen gas**. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Neutralization Reaction:**
 
 
• The reaction **NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H2O** is a **neutralization reaction** occurring between a **strong base (Sodium Hydroxide)** and a **strong acid (Hydrochloric Acid)**.
 
• The products are **Sodium Chloride** (a soluble salt) and **Water**. No precipitate is formed in this specific reaction as all products remain in the aqueous phase or as liquid water. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Applications:** Precipitation reactions are used in **wastewater treatment** to remove **heavy metals** or **phosphates** from water by turning them into solid precipitates that can be easily filtered out.
 
• **Ionic Equation:** The **net ionic equation** for the correct answer is **Ag+(aq) + Cl-(aq) → AgCl(s)**, which focuses only on the species that actually change during the reaction.

questions.question: If an object is moving in a straight line and covers a distance of 10 km from point A to point B, then which of the following statements is true regarding the displacement of the object from point A to point B?

options.text: Displacement will be equal to 10 km.
Displacement will always be less than 10 km.
Displacement will be more than 10 km.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**displacement will be equal to 10 km**__ .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Displacement** is defined as the shortest straight distance between **the initial position** and **the final position** of an object .
 
• When an object moves in a **straight line** from **point A to ****point B and does not change its direction, then the magnitude of ****distance** covered and **displacement** is equal.
 
• Since the question states that the object travels a distance of **10 km** in a straight line, the displacement between **point A** and **point B** will also be exactly **10 km . *****Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Displacement is always less than **10 km** only when the object moves along a curved or zigzag path. Here, the path is straight. ***Therefore, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **The magnitude of displacement can never be greater** than the distance traveled , as it is the shortest path between two points. ***Therefore, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• Displacement is **zero** only when the object returns to the same starting point after starting its journey. ***Therefore, statement 2 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Distance:**

 
 
• It is **the total path length of the actual path** covered by a moving object .
 
• Distance is a **scalar quantity** , which has only magnitude and no definite direction.
 
• Distance is always **positive** and can never be zero or negative if the object has moved.
 
 
 
• **Displacement:**
 
 
• It is a **vector quantity** , which means it has both **magnitude** and **direction .**
 
• The value of displacement can be **positive, negative or zero .**
 
• Its **SI unit** is the metre (m), although for larger distances **the kilometre (km)** is used.
 
 
 
• **Relation between distance and displacement:**
 
 
• For any moving object, **the distance is always equal to or greater than the magnitude of displacement** (Distance ≥ |Displacement|).
 
• If an object moves on **a circular path** and completes one revolution, then the distance will be **2πr** , but the displacement will be **0 .**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Uniform Motion:** If an object travels equal distances in equal intervals of time along a straight line, it is said to have uniform motion. In this case, **velocity** and **speed** remain the same.
 
• **Example of zero displacement: If you go to school ****5 km** away from your home and come back home, your total distance will be **10 km** , but your total displacement will be **0 km** because your initial and final position are the same.
 
• **Negative displacement:** Displacement can be negative if the object moves in a direction opposite to the chosen reference direction.
 
• **Year 1687:** Sir **Isaac Newton** explained in detail the laws of motion and principles like displacement in his book **'Principia' .**

questions.question: Which of the following processes represents the most specific purpose of meiotic cell division?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**प्रजनन**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meiosis** is a specialized form of **cell division** that reduces the **chromosome number** by half, resulting in the production of four **haploid** daughter cells.
 
• The most specific and fundamental purpose of **meiotic division** is to facilitate **reproduction (प्रजनन)**, specifically sexual reproduction, by creating **gametes** (sperm and egg cells).
 
• This process ensures that when **fertilization** occurs, the resulting **zygote** has the correct **diploid** number of chromosomes, maintaining chromosomal stability across generations.
 
• In contrast, options such as **digestion (पाचन)**, **respiration (श्वसन)**, and **excretion ( उत्सर्जन)** are physiological and metabolic processes handled by organ systems and do not involve this specific type of cell division.
 
• During **Meiosis**, genetic material is shuffled through **crossing over**, which creates **genetic diversity** among offspring, a key driver of **evolution**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Reproduction.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Stages of Meiosis**:

 
 
• **Meiosis I**: Known as **reductional division**, it involves the separation of **homologous chromosomes**. It includes phases like **Prophase I**, **Metaphase I**, **Anaphase I**, and **Telophase I**.
 
• **Meiosis II**: Known as **equational division**, it is similar to **mitosis** where **sister chromatids** are separated into four **haploid** cells.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Mitosis**:
 
 
• While **Meiosis** is for **reproduction** and occurs in **germ cells**, **Mitosis** occurs in **somatic cells** for the purpose of **growth**, **tissue repair**, and **asexual reproduction**.
 
• **Mitosis** produces two genetically identical **diploid** daughter cells, whereas Meiosis produces four genetically different **haploid** cells.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Crossing Over**:
 
 
• Occurring during **Pachytene** of **Prophase I**, **crossing over** is the exchange of genetic material between non-sister chromatids, ensuring that no two gametes are exactly alike.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Discovery**: Meiosis was first discovered and described in sea urchin eggs by the German biologist **Oscar Hertwig** in **1876**.
 
• **Location**: In humans and other animals, this process takes place in the **gonads**—the **testes** in males and the **ovaries** in females.
 
• **Numerical Value**: In humans, meiosis reduces the **46 chromosomes** (23 pairs) of a **diploid** cell to **23 chromosomes** in a **haploid** gamete.
 
• **Aneuploidy**: Errors during meiosis, such as **non-disjunction** (failure of chromosomes to separate), can lead to chromosomal abnormalities like **Down Syndrome** (Trisomy **21**).

questions.question: Which type of molecule of an element contains only one type of atom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**एकपरमाणुक**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atomicity** is defined as the total number of atoms present in one molecule of an element or a compound. Based on this, molecules are classified as monoatomic, diatomic, triatomic, or polyatomic.
 
• An **एकपरमाणुक** (**Monoatomic**) molecule is one that consists of only **one atom**. Such elements are stable enough to exist independently without bonding to another atom of the same type.
 
• The most prominent examples of monoatomic elements are the **Noble Gases** found in **Group 18** of the **Periodic Table**. These include **Helium (He)**, **Neon (Ne)**, **Argon (Ar)**, **Krypton (Kr)**, **Xenon (Xe)**, and **Radon (Rn)**.
 
• These gases remain monoatomic because they possess a **complete valence shell** (octet or duet configuration), which makes them chemically inert and highly stable under standard conditions.
 
• Many **metals**, such as **Sodium (Na)**, **Iron (Fe)**, **Copper (Cu)**, and **Aluminium (Al)**, are also typically represented as monoatomic in chemical equations and formulas, although they exist in a metallic lattice structure in their solid state. ***Hence, the option for monoatomic is the correct answer.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Diatomic Molecules (द्विपरमाणुक)**:

 
 
• These molecules are composed of exactly **two atoms** of the same or different chemical elements.
 
• Examples of diatomic elements include **Hydrogen (H2)**, **Nitrogen (N2)**, **Oxygen (O2)**, **Fluorine (F2)**, **Chlorine (Cl2)**, **Bromine (Br2)**, and **Iodine (I2)**.
 
 
 
• **Triatomic Molecules (त्रिपरमाणुक)**:
 
 
• These consist of **three atoms** bonded together.
 
• A common example of a triatomic elemental molecule is **Ozone (O3)**, which is an allotrope of oxygen. Compounds like **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)** and **Water (H2O)** are also triatomic but are considered molecules of compounds rather than elements.
 
 
 
• **Polyatomic Molecules (बहुपरमाणुक)**:
 
 
• These contain **more than three atoms**.
 
• **Phosphorus** usually exists as a **tetraatomic** molecule (**P4**), while **Sulphur** exists as an **octatomic** molecule (**S8**).
 
• Carbon in the form of **Fullerene (C60)** is another example of a complex polyatomic structure.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Atomicity**:
 
 
• Atomicity helps in determining the **molecular mass** of an element and is essential for balancing **chemical equations**.
 
• It reflects the **chemical bonding** behavior of the atoms, where non-metals typically form diatomic or polyatomic molecules to share **valence electrons** and reach a stable state.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The term **Molecule of an Element** specifically refers to molecules containing atoms of only **one type** of element, such as **O2** or **S8**.
 
• The **Noble Gases** are the only elements that are naturally found in a stable, gaseous **monoatomic** state at room **temperature** and **pressure**.
 
• The **Atomic Number** of the element does not determine its atomicity; rather, it is the **electron configuration** and the tendency to form **covalent bonds** that dictates how many atoms will cluster together to form a molecule.

questions.question: Which of the following is a form of mechanical energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kinetic energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mechanical energy** is defined as the energy possessed by an object due to its **motion** or its **stored energy of position**.
 
• It is the sum of two types of energy: **Potential Energy** and **Kinetic Energy**.
 
• **Kinetic energy** (**गतिज ऊर्जा**) is the energy an object has because of its **motion**. Any object that is moving, whether it is a **rolling ball** or a **speeding car**, possesses kinetic energy. ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***
 
• **Sound energy** (**ध्वनि ऊर्जा**) is the form of energy generated by the **vibrations** of matter. While it involves movement of particles, it is categorized as a separate form of energy in classical mechanics. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Chemical energy** (**रासायनिक ऊर्जा**) is the energy stored in the **bonds** of chemical compounds, such as **atoms and molecules**. It is a form of **potential energy** but is usually classified under chemical processes rather than pure mechanical systems. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Heat energy** (**ऊष्मा ऊर्जा**) or **Thermal energy** is the internal energy of a system due to the **random motion** of its atoms and molecules. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy (KE):**

 
 
• The **formula** for calculating kinetic energy is **KE = 1/2 mv²**, where **m** represents the **mass** of the object and **v** represents its **velocity**.
 
• Since **velocity** is squared in the formula, doubling the speed of an object will **quadruple** its kinetic energy.
 
• The **SI unit** of kinetic energy is the **Joule (J)**, named after the physicist **James Prescott Joule**.
 
 
 
• **Potential Energy (PE):**
 
 
• This is **stored energy** based on an object's **position** or **configuration**.
 
• **Gravitational Potential Energy** is calculated using the formula **PE = mgh**, where **g** is the **acceleration due to gravity** (approximately **9.8 m/s²**) and **h** is the **height**.
 
• Examples include a **stretched rubber band** (Elastic Potential Energy) or water stored behind a **dam**.
 
 
 
• **Law of Conservation of Energy:**
 
 
• Energy can neither be **created nor destroyed**; it can only be **transformed** from one form to another.
 
• In a frictionless environment, the **Total Mechanical Energy** (KE + PE) of a system remains **constant**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Scalar Quantity:** Both **mechanical energy** and its components (KE and PE) are **scalar quantities**, meaning they have **magnitude** but no **direction**.
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem:** This theorem states that the **net work done** on an object is equal to the **change** in its **kinetic energy**.
 
• **Applications:** Mechanical energy is utilized in various technologies like **wind turbines** (converting kinetic energy of wind to electricity) and **hydroelectric power plants** (using the potential energy of water).
 
• **Examples of Mechanical Energy:** A **flying airplane** possesses both kinetic energy (due to its speed) and potential energy (due to its altitude). A **hammer** being swung to hit a nail possesses kinetic energy that does **work** on the nail.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms aids in the pollination of flowers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Honey bee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pollination** is the biological process of transferring **pollen grains** from the male part of a flower (**anther**) to the female part (**stigma**), enabling **fertilization** and the production of **seeds**.
 
• **Honey bees** (genus **Apis**) are the most prominent and effective **biotic agents** of pollination in the ecosystem.
 
• While foraging for **nectar** and **pollen** to feed their colony, bees inadvertently pick up pollen on their **body hairs**; this pollen is then deposited on the **stigma** of the next flower they visit.
 
• It is estimated that **honey bees** are responsible for approximately **80%** of all **insect-led pollination**, making them vital for the production of **commercial crops** such as **almonds**, **apples**, and **sunflowers**.
 
• Bees exhibit **floral fidelity**, meaning they tend to visit the same species of flowers during a single trip, which significantly increases the efficiency of **cross-pollination**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Honey bee.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Euglena:**

 
 
• **Euglena** is a genus of **single-celled flagellated microorganisms** that possess characteristics of both **plants** (contain **chloroplasts** for photosynthesis) and **animals** (can ingest food).
 
• They are typically found in **freshwater** and **saltwater** environments and do not play any role in the **reproduction** or **pollination** of flowering plants.
 
 
 
• **Plasmodium:**
 
 
• **Plasmodium** is a genus of **unicellular protozoan parasites**.
 
• They are best known as the causative agents of **Malaria** in humans and are transmitted via the bite of an infected female **Anopheles mosquito**.
 
• They exist as **obligate parasites** and have no ecological function related to **plant pollination**.
 
 
 
• **Amoeba:**
 
 
• An **Amoeba** is a highly **malleable unicellular organism** belonging to the kingdom **Protista**.
 
• It moves and captures food using temporary cytoplasmic projections called **pseudopodia** (false feet).
 
• Like **Euglena** and **Plasmodium**, it is an aquatic or soil-dwelling microorganism with no involvement in **floral biology**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Types of Pollination:**

 
 
• **Self-pollination:** Occurs when pollen from the **anther** is deposited on the **stigma** of the same flower or another flower on the **same plant**.
 
• **Cross-pollination:** Occurs when pollen is transferred from the **anther** of one plant to the **stigma** of a **different plant** of the same species, promoting **genetic diversity**.
 
 
 
• **Agents of Pollination:**
 
 
• **Biotic Agents:** These include **insects** (bees, butterflies, beetles), **birds** (hummingbirds), and **mammals** (bats). Pollination by insects is specifically termed **Entomophily**.
 
• **Abiotic Agents:** These include **wind** (Anemophily) and **water** (Hydrophily). Wind-pollinated plants, like **grasses** and **maize**, produce large quantities of light, non-sticky pollen.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:** The **Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)** highlights that pollinators like **bees** affect **35 percent** of the world's **crop production**, increasing the outputs of **87** of the leading **food crops** worldwide.

questions.question: When calcium carbonate is heated, it produces calcium oxide and carbon dioxide. This is an example of which type of chemical reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**अपघटन**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• कैल्शियम कार्बोनेट (**CaCO3**) को गर्म करने पर इसका कैल्शियम ऑक्साइड (**CaO**) और कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड (**CO2**) में परिवर्तन **अपघटन अभिक्रिया** (Decomposition Reaction) का एक उत्कृष्ट उदाहरण है।
 
• **अपघटन अभिक्रिया** वह रासायनिक प्रक्रिया है जिसमें एक **एकल अभिकारक** ऊष्मा, प्रकाश या विद्युत जैसी ऊर्जा के प्रभाव में टूटकर दो या दो से अधिक सरल उत्पाद बनाता है।
 
• चूँकि इस विशिष्ट अभिक्रिया में कैल्शियम कार्बोनेट को तोड़ने के लिए **ऊष्मा** (Heat) का उपयोग किया जाता है, इसलिए इसे **तापीय अपघटन** (Thermal Decomposition) कहा जाता है।
 
• इस अभिक्रिया का रासायनिक समीकरण इस प्रकार है: **CaCO3 (s) → CaO (s) + CO2 (g)**। यहाँ **CaCO3** चूना पत्थर (Limestone) है और **CaO** बिना बुझा हुआ चूना (Quicklime) है।
 
• यह अभिक्रिया औद्योगिक रूप से अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि उत्पादित **कैल्शियम ऑक्साइड** का उपयोग **सीमेंट** के निर्माण में बड़े पैमाने पर किया जाता है।

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **संयोजन अभिक्रिया (Combination Reaction):**

 
 
• यह अपघटन के विपरीत होती है। इसमें दो या दो से अधिक **तत्व या यौगिक** मिलकर एक **एकल उत्पाद** बनाते हैं।
 
• उदाहरण के लिए, जब कोयला (कार्बन) ऑक्सीजन में जलता है: **C + O2 → CO2**।
 
 
 
• **विस्थापन अभिक्रिया (Displacement Reaction):**
 
 
• इस अभिक्रिया में एक **अधिक अभिक्रियाशील** तत्व किसी कम अभिक्रियाशील तत्व को उसके जलीय विलयन से **विस्थापित** कर देता है।
 
• उदाहरण: जब लोहे की कील को कॉपर सल्फेट के घोल में डाला जाता है, तो लोहा कॉपर को हटा देता है: **Fe + CuSO4 → FeSO4 + Cu**।
 
 
 
• **दोहरी विस्थापन अभिक्रिया (Double Displacement Reaction):**
 
 
• इसमें दो अलग-अलग यौगिकों के बीच **आयनों का आदान-प्रदान** होता है, जिससे दो नए यौगिक बनते हैं।
 
• अक्सर इसमें एक **अवक्षेप** (Precipitate) बनता है। उदाहरण: **Na2SO4 + BaCl2 → BaSO4 + 2NaCl**।
 
 
 
• **ऊष्माशोषी और ऊष्माक्षेपी अभिक्रियाएं:**
 
 
• **अपघटन अभिक्रियाएं** आमतौर पर **ऊष्माशोषी** (Endothermic) होती हैं क्योंकि उन्हें बंधन तोड़ने के लिए ऊर्जा के अवशोषण की आवश्यकता होती है।
 
• इसके विपरीत, जिन अभिक्रियाओं में ऊर्जा बाहर निकलती है, उन्हें **ऊष्माक्षेपी** (Exothermic) कहा जाता है, जैसे श्वसन या प्राकृतिक गैस का जलना।
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **अपघटन के प्रकार:** अपघटन केवल ऊष्मा से ही नहीं होता। यदि यह **विद्युत** द्वारा किया जाता है (जैसे पानी का इलेक्ट्रोलिसिस), तो इसे **विद्युत अपघटन** कहते हैं। यदि यह **सूर्य के प्रकाश** द्वारा किया जाता है (जैसे सिल्वर क्लोराइड का धूसर होना), तो इसे **प्रकाशीय अपघटन** कहा जाता है।
 
• **कैल्शियम कार्बोनेट के स्रोत:** प्रकृति में यह **चूना पत्थर**, **खड़िया** (Chalk) और **संगमरमर** (Marble) के रूप में पाया जाता है। इन सभी का रासायनिक सूत्र **CaCO3** ही होता है।

• चूँकि इस विशिष्ट अभिक्रिया में कैल्शियम कार्बोनेट को तोड़ने के लिए **ऊष्मा** (Heat) का उपयोग किया जाता है, इसलिए इसे **तापीय अपघटन** (Thermal Decomposition) कहा जाता है।
 
• इस अभिक्रिया का रासायनिक समीकरण इस प्रकार है: **CaCO3 (s) → CaO (s) + CO2 (g)**। यहाँ **CaCO3** चूना पत्थर (Limestone) है और **CaO** बिना बुझा हुआ चूना (Quicklime) है।

questions.question: Which type of muscular tissue is present in the wall of the stomach?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Smooth muscle tissue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Smooth muscle tissue** is the type of muscle found in the walls of **hollow visceral organs** such as the **stomach**, **intestines**, **urinary bladder**, and **blood vessels**.
 
• These muscles are characterized as **involuntary muscles** because their movements cannot be consciously controlled by the individual; they are regulated by the **Autonomic Nervous System (ANS)**.
 
• In the **stomach**, the smooth muscle layers are responsible for **peristalsis** and the **mechanical churning** of food, which aids in breaking down food particles and mixing them with **gastric juices**.
 
• The structure of smooth muscle cells is **spindle-shaped** (fusiform), with a **single, centrally located nucleus**, and they lack the **striations** (cross-bands) seen in skeletal or cardiac muscles. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• The **stomach wall** is unique as it typically contains **three layers** of smooth muscle: the **inner oblique**, **middle circular**, and **outer longitudinal** layers, which provide the multidirectional strength needed for digestion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Skeletal Muscle Tissue**:

 
 
• These are **voluntary muscles** that are under the conscious control of the **Somatic Nervous System**.
 
• They are primarily attached to **bones** via **tendons** and are responsible for **locomotion** and body posture.
 
• Structurally, they are **striated** (striped) and contain **multiple nuclei** located at the periphery of the long, cylindrical cells. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Cardiac Muscle Tissue**:
 
 
• This specialized tissue is found exclusively in the **heart** (specifically the **myocardium**).
 
• Like smooth muscle, it is **involuntary**, but like skeletal muscle, it is **striated**.
 
• Cardiac muscle cells are **branched** and joined by **intercalated discs**, which allow for rapid transmission of electrical impulses for synchronized heart contractions. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Fluid Connective Tissue**:
 
 
• This is a category of **connective tissue** rather than muscular tissue.
 
• It includes **blood** and **lymph**, which circulate through the body to transport **nutrients**, **oxygen**, **hormones**, and **waste products**.
 
• It does not possess the contractile properties required to move the walls of the stomach. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Muscular System Overview**: The human body contains over **600 muscles**, categorized into three types based on their **location**, **structure**, and **function**.
 
• **Functional Differences**: While **skeletal muscles** fatigue quickly and require rest, **smooth muscles** (like those in the **digestive tract**) can maintain **prolonged contractions** without tiring easily, which is essential for the slow process of digestion.
 
• **Microscopic Appearance**: **Smooth muscle** is called "smooth" specifically because it lacks the **sarcomere** arrangement that creates the **striated** appearance in **skeletal** and **cardiac** tissues.
 
• **Role in Homeostasis**: Beyond the stomach, smooth muscles play a critical role in **regulating blood pressure** by altering the diameter of **arteries** and controlling the flow of air in the **bronchioles** of the **lungs**.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**किसी तरल में दाब पात्र की आकृति पर निर्भर करता है**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **दाब (Pressure)** को प्रति इकाई क्षेत्रफल पर लगने वाले **लंबवत बल (Thrust)** के रूप में परिभाषित किया जाता है। इसका गणितीय सूत्र **दाब = बल / क्षेत्रफल** होता है। ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• किसी शांत तरल (static fluid) के भीतर किसी बिंदु पर **दाब सभी दिशाओं में समान रूप से** कार्य करता है। यह **पास्कल के नियम (Pascal's Law)** के मूलभूत सिद्धांतों में से एक है। ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• किसी तरल स्तंभ के कारण उत्पन्न दाब केवल तरल के **घनत्व (Density)**, **गुरुत्वीय त्वरण (Gravity)** और मुक्त सतह से उसकी **गहराई (Depth)** पर निर्भर करता है। यह **पात्र की आकृति (Shape of the container)** या आकार पर निर्भर नहीं करता है। इसे **द्रवस्थैतिक विरोधाभास (Hydrostatic Paradox)** भी कहा जाता है। ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• जैसे-जैसे तरल में नीचे की ओर जाते हैं, ऊपर स्थित तरल के भार के कारण **दाब गहराई के साथ रैखिक रूप से बढ़ता है**। सूत्र **P = hρg** के अनुसार, गहराई (h) बढ़ने पर दाब (P) बढ़ता है। ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• ***अतः, सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 है क्योंकि यह कथन गलत है।***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **पास्कल का नियम (Pascal's Law):**

 
 
• यह नियम **ब्लेज पास्कल** द्वारा **1647** में दिया गया था। इसके अनुसार, एक बंद तरल पर लगाया गया दाब बिना किसी कमी के तरल के हर हिस्से और पात्र की दीवारों पर संचरित होता है।
 
• इसका उपयोग **हाइड्रोलिक लिफ्ट (Hydraulic Lift)**, **हाइड्रोलिक जैक** और वाहनों के **हाइड्रोलिक ब्रेक** में किया जाता है।
 
 
 
• **दाब की इकाइयाँ (Units of Pressure):**
 
 
• दाब की **SI इकाई** **पास्कल (Pa)** है, जिसे **1 न्यूटन प्रति वर्ग मीटर (N/m²)** के रूप में भी जाना जाता है।
 
• अन्य सामान्य इकाइयों में **एटमोस्फीयर (atm)**, **बार (bar)** और **टॉर (torr)** शामिल हैं। **1 bar** का मान **100,000 पास्कल** के बराबर होता है।
 
 
 
• **द्रवस्थैतिक दाब (Hydrostatic Pressure):**
 
 
• किसी तरल के अंदर **गहराई 'h'** पर कुल दाब **P = P0 + hρg** होता है, जहाँ **P0 वायुमंडलीय दाब** है।
 
• यह दाब तरल के **आयतन** या पात्र के **आधार क्षेत्र** पर निर्भर नहीं करता, बल्कि केवल ऊर्ध्वाधर ऊंचाई पर निर्भर करता है।
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **अदिश राशि (Scalar Quantity):**

 
 
• दाब एक **अदिश राशि** है क्योंकि किसी बिंदु पर यह सभी दिशाओं में समान होता है, इसकी कोई विशिष्ट दिशा नहीं होती है।
 
 
 
• **वायुमंडलीय दाब (Atmospheric Pressure):**
 
 
• समुद्र तल पर मानक वायुमंडलीय दाब लगभग **101,325 Pa** या **1 atm** होता है। इसे मापने के लिए **बैरोमीटर (Barometer)** का उपयोग किया जाता है, जिसका आविष्कार **टॉरिसिली** ने किया था।
 
• ऊंचाई बढ़ने पर (जैसे पहाड़ों पर) वायुमंडलीय दाब **कम** हो जाता है, जिससे तरल का क्वथनांक भी कम हो जाता है।
